title: The Peace of Augsburg lets German princes choose their faith
summary: Charles V's brother Ferdinand and the princes of the Empire agreed that each ruler could choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his territory.
reason: Decades of religious conflict and the Schmalkaldic War had shown that the Lutherans could not be suppressed by force.
significance: It brought sixty years of relative peace to Germany and fixed the principle that the ruler decides the religion.
